hook: Your satellite view of the Sahara shows a bullseye.
title: A 40 km Bullseye Sits in the Sahara
description:
Zoom into the Sahara on a satellite map and you will find a giant ring pattern called the Richat Structure. It is about 40 km wide in Mauritania. Scientists say it is eroded rock layers. Part of the Places That Shouldn't Exist series.

#Shorts #Sahara #Geography
comment_prompt: Crater or not? Crater or rock

scenes.narration: Your satellite view of the Sahara shows a bullseye.
scenes.headline: SAHARA BULLSEYE

scenes.narration: It is called the Richat Structure.
scenes.headline: RICHAT STRUCTURE

scenes.narration: That is big enough to spot from orbit.
scenes.headline: SEEN FROM ORBIT

scenes.narration: Astronauts used it as a landmark.
scenes.headline: ASTRONAUT LANDMARK

scenes.narration: It sits in the desert of Mauritania.
scenes.headline: MAURITANIA DESERT

scenes.narration: For years people called it a crater.
scenes.headline: NOT A CRATER

scenes.narration: Scientists say it is rock layers worn away.
scenes.headline: ERODED ROCK LAYERS

scenes.narration: Your Sahara bullseye is real, and it is rock.
scenes.headline: REAL AND ROCK
